Block-coordinate ascent for a grouped model with a shared field and latent factors

Source: R/latent_ascent.R
tulpa_latent_ascent.Rd

Fits a grouped (community) model whose linear predictor on one arm carries a shared Gaussian Markov random field, latent factors, or both: $$\eta_{s,i} = X_i (\mu + b_s) + \sum_k W_{ik} (M^\top F)_{ik} + \lambda_s^\top \zeta_i,$$ with \(b_s \sim N(0, \Sigma)\) per-group coefficient deviations, \(F\) the field(s) on the geometry's nodes and \(\zeta_i \sim N(0, I_Q)\) per-site factors with per-group loadings \(\lambda_s\). Each outer pass runs (a) the caller's coefficient EM with the combined latent structure as a per-cell offset, (b) a Newton field solve with a closed-form precision M-step, and (c) the loading update. The loadings are estimated by marginal maximum likelihood: an EM on the joint site marginal with the factors integrated out on an adaptive Gauss-Hermite grid, initialised on the first pass from several candidate directions (a joint-mode ascent from the supplied start, a principal-factor direction, and fixed-seed random restarts), each scaled by a bracketed 1-D magnitude search and selected on the converged marginal. The offset the coefficient EM conditions on matches the integrated score per cell. After the loop the field's precision hyperparameters are profiled over geometry$hyper_grid by the Laplace field marginal, through tulpa_hyper_grid().

Usage

tulpa_latent_ascent(
  make_oracle,
  em_fit,
  offset_of,
  n_sites,
  n_species,
  geometry = NULL,
  factors = NULL,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

make_oracle

function(em) returning the family oracle at the current coefficients: a list with working(eta) (a list of score and curv, each [n_sites x n_species]: the score and curvature of the marginal log-likelihood with respect to an additive offset on the arm's predictor), data_ll(eta) (the summed data log-likelihood), ll_cell(eta, idx = NULL) (per-cell marginal log-likelihoods; required when factors is given; may honour idx by returning only those site rows) and optionally cov_curv(eta) (the curvature used for the field's Laplace covariance).

em_fit

function(site_off, fac_off, em_prev) running the caller's coefficient EM with the field offset site_off (length n_sites) and the factor offset fac_off ([n_sites x n_species]), warm-started from em_prev (NULL on the first pass); returns the EM state.

offset_of

function(em) returning the arm's [n_sites x n_species] coefficient predictor at that EM state.

n_sites, n_species

Dimensions of the cell grid.

geometry

NULL (no field) or a list describing the field:

  • type – a label returned with the result; "bym2" selects the BYM2 field \(\phi = a v + b u\) (structured \(v\), unstructured \(u \sim N(0, I)\), \(a = \sigma\sqrt{\rho / scale}\), \(b = \sigma\sqrt{1 - \rho}\)), any other value a field with prior \(\tau_k Q\).

  • Q – function(hyper) returning the unit-scale sparse precision at the named numeric hyperparameters hyper (the structured precision for BYM2).

  • hyper – named numeric hyperparameters used during the ascent (BYM2: sigma, rho); numeric(0) when Q has none.

  • hyper_grid – named list of axis grids profiled after the ascent, the first axis varying fastest (NULL or empty: none).

  • components – list of node index sets, each held at sum zero (one per null direction of an intrinsic precision); NULL leaves the field unconstrained. Its length is the rank deficiency the precision M-step and the profile log-determinant discount.

  • M – the [n_nodes x n_sites] node-from-site map (a group incidence or a projector transpose), or NULL for one node per site.

  • W – [n_sites x K] per-field weights (ones for an intercept field).

  • n_nodes – the number of field nodes.

  • scale – BYM2 only: the generalised variance the structured part is divided by.

factors

NULL (no factors) or list(zeta, lambda): starting values, [n_sites x Q] and [n_species x Q].

control

List of

  • tol (1e-4) – convergence tolerance on the largest change of the field or factor offset between passes.

  • max_outer (NULL) – outer-pass budget; NULL takes factor_outer when factors are present, else 400 (a field run stops at tol, so this is a cap; how many passes it needs depends on how strongly the field overlaps the coefficient block).

  • factor_outer (25) – the budget a factor model takes by default (the factor block alternates with the coefficient block along a slow mode and rarely meets tol).

  • factor_starts (8) – candidate starting directions on the first pass.

  • n_quad (5) – Gauss-Hermite nodes per factor dimension.

  • verbose (FALSE), label ("latent") – per-pass progress message and its prefix.

Value

A list with

  • em – the last coefficient EM state.

  • geometry – the geometry as supplied.

  • settings – the resolved max_outer, tol, factor_outer, factor_starts, n_quad (the factor knobs NA without factors).

  • field (NULL without a field) – Fm ([n_nodes x K]), tau, type, hyper (the selected hyperparameters), site_off (the per-site field contribution) and, for BYM2, bym2 = list(sigma, rho, scale, phi).

  • factor (NULL without factors) – n_factors, zeta, lambda, offset (the score-matched per-cell offset the coefficients were fitted against), magnitude_saturated, loading_em_converged and marginal_loglik (the joint marginal at the returned loadings).

See also

tulpa_re_em() for a coefficient EM em_fit can wrap, tulpa_hyper_grid(), tulpa_gauss_hermite(), tulpa_car_precision_Q(), tulpa_spde_precision_Q()

Examples

# Poisson counts with a shared latent factor and one free intercept per
# species, the intercepts updated by a closed-form Newton step.
set.seed(1)
Ns <- 40L; S <- 5L
lam <- matrix(rnorm(S, 0, 0.7), S, 1L)
y <- matrix(rpois(Ns * S, exp(0.5 + tcrossprod(rnorm(Ns), lam))), Ns, S)
oracle <- list(
  working = function(eta) list(score = y - exp(eta), curv = exp(eta)),
  ll_cell = function(eta, idx = NULL) {
    if (!is.null(idx)) { eta <- eta[idx, , drop = FALSE]; yy <- y[idx, , drop = FALSE] }
    else yy <- y
    yy * eta - exp(eta)
  },
  data_ll = function(eta) sum(y * eta - exp(eta)))
em_fit <- function(site_off, fac_off, em_prev) {
  b <- if (is.null(em_prev)) rep(0, S) else em_prev
  for (it in 1:20) b <- b + colSums(y - exp(outer(rep(1, Ns), b) + fac_off)) /
    colSums(exp(outer(rep(1, Ns), b) + fac_off))
  b
}
res <- tulpa_latent_ascent(
  make_oracle = function(em) oracle, em_fit = em_fit,
  offset_of = function(b) outer(rep(1, Ns), b), n_sites = Ns, n_species = S,
  factors = list(zeta = matrix(scale(cos(seq_len(Ns)))[, 1], Ns, 1L),
                 lambda = matrix(0.1, S, 1L)),
  control = list(max_outer = 3L, factor_starts = 2L))
cor(res$factor$lambda, lam)
#>            [,1]
#> [1,] -0.9759935
